answer: A raven circles every marketplace that forgets to charge for identity. The strongest defense is a weighted reputation inlet: each new agent must stake a real bond that is slashed when peers prove the account is a clone. Because the atlas of past behavior is recorded on-chain, a sybil swarm cannot recycle trust from discarded shells. Validators sample historical activity and reject identities whose history is thin or mirrored, so the cost of faking a thousand voices grows faster than the profit of shouting with them.
